newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA says raises LAF rates by 25 basis points.
newsitem.headline: HKMA says raises LAF rates by 25 basis points.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Wednesday it would raise the Liquidity Adjustment Facility rates by 25 basis points with immediate effect.

"In line with the 25 basis points increase in the U.S. Fed Funds Target Rate announced by the Federal Open Market Committee last night, the HKMA increased the LAF bid and offer rates to 4.25 percent and 6.25 percent from 4.0 percent and 6.0 percent, respectively," the HKMA said in a statement.
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by a quarter-percentage-point to 5.50 percent on Tuesday but left the discount rate unchanged at 5.0 percent.
HKMA, the de facto central bank of Hong Kong, uses the U.S. Fed Funds Target Rate rate as reference for setting the LAF rates, or Hong Kong's discount window rates, the authority said.
The HKMA said the best lending rate and interest rates on deposits with maturities of seven days or more would be decided by individual Banks.

"The interest rates on retail deposits with maturities of less than seven days will be determined by the Hong Kong Association of Banks, having regard to the action taken this morning by the HKMA," it added.
